newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates higher on governor's appeal.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates higher on governor's appeal.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates edged higher at the close on Wednesday following central bank Governor Sheu Yuan-dong's comment on Tuesday that the overnight interbank rate was too low, dealers said.

The interbank rate ended at 4.935 percent against Tuesday's 4.568 close, very close to the five percent level that Sheu, in comments to reporters, said he hoped for. The 30-day commercial paper closed at 4.75-4.85 percent against 4.60-4.70.
Dealers said they expected the rates to edge above 5.00 percent on Thursday.
Sheu had said he hoped the overnight money rate would rise to five percent, saying investors' interests would be hurt if liquidity became too loose.

The government bond market reported no transaction in the afternoon amid caution over Sheu's comments, but traders said liquidity in the banking system was stable and that they did not expect major movements in the yields.
A consolidation phase was likely to continue in the bond market in coming sessions, traders said.
